content.body:
Found in the review of #162 (finding 3 in https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/pull/162#issuecomment-6050269233), and older than that PR.

`collect` in `crates/ascribe-fmt/src/files.rs` follows linked folders without remembering which folders it has already visited. A link back up the tree, such as `docs/loop -> .`, makes `fmt` walk the same folders again and again until the path gets too long. With such a link, `fmt --check` lists each file about 40 times, prints ASC123 about 40 times, and reports "41 files would be reformatted". For the same project, `ascribe check` reports each file once.

What a fix needs: remember the canonical folders already visited, as `FileSystem::sources` does (`Walk` in `crates/ascribe-resolve/src/fs.rs`), so each folder is walked once. It changes behavior, so it comes with a test (in `crates/ascribe-cli/tests/fmt.rs`, using `tests/support/links.rs`, since a conformance case can't hold a link) and a changelog line.
content.title: `ascribe fmt` follows a linked folder that loops back into the content root

`design/tokens.toml` names a palette step by its lightness: 1000 × (1 − OKLCH L). `design/candidates/chosen.toml` names steps 50 to 975 instead. So the same color has two names, for example `indigo.435` and `indigo.600` for `#5962e8`. A test holds the shared colors equal, so a contributor who changes a shared color has to find the same hex under a different name in each file. `design/README.md` explains this for now (#179).

Choose one naming and use it in both files. Better still, generate one file from the other, since the assets and the specimen read `chosen.toml` and the stylesheets read `tokens.toml`.

content.body:
Found in the agents pass (phase 11, #202; `project-docs/agents/pass-results.md`).

On a project with a few hundred warnings, `ascribe check --summary` shows which rules to work through, but nothing narrows `check` to one code. `--format concise` cuts at 50 lines, and its "and N more:" command narrows by file, not by rule. So an agent (or a person) can't fix one rule across the whole project from the concise output; it ends up working file by file.

Proposal to design: a `--code <code-or-slug>` filter on `ascribe check` (repeatable), applied after the check like the path filter, and the same argument on the MCP tool `ascribe_check`. When the concise list is cut, its "next" command would keep the filter. Open questions: whether `--summary` should suggest it, and how it interacts with `--format prompt`.
content.title: Let `ascribe check` narrow to one diagnostic code, for fixing one rule at a time

content.body:
Found in the agents pass (phase 11, #202; `project-docs/agents/pass-results.md`).

`ascribe agents hook <agent> --event stop` holds an agent only while there are errors (agents decision 12, phase 9). A project whose CI runs `ascribe check --deny-warnings`, as Getting started suggests, can still have the agent finish with warnings, which then fail CI.

To design: how a project says its warnings count, so the stop hook holds on them too. Options: a setting in `ascribe.toml` (which `check` could also read), an option on the hook command that `agents sync --with-hook` writes, or leaving it as is. Worth deciding after the hand runs in `project-docs/agents/hand-checks.md` show whether agents leave warnings behind.
content.title: The agents' stop hook lets an agent finish with warnings

## What

`packages/cli/src/binary.ts:56` exports `nativeBinaryPath`, described as a "backwards-compatible name for resolveBinary". At version 0.2.0 there is no installed base to be compatible with, so the alias is redundant.

## Where

- `packages/cli/src/binary.ts:56` — the alias itself
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts:7` — re-exports it from the package
- `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts:2,40,53` — the only consumers, its own tests

## Why remove it

The project is greenfield (0.x, `publish = false` workspace, first releases); nothing outside this repo can depend on the old name. `resolveBinary` already covers the use case, with an options object instead of two positional arguments.

## Notes

A sweep for legacy/migration code (legacy markers, fallbacks, shims, unused deps via `cargo machete`, unused workspace members) found no other candidates; the MCP `LEGACY` protocol versions and the retired `ASC039` slug are recorded decisions, not bloat. This alias was the only actionable item.
content.title: Remove the backwards-compat alias nativeBinaryPath in @ascribed/cli

content.body:
## What happens

`ascribe report links` runs lychee and reads its JSON. lychee also reads the project's own `lychee.toml`, which the [report guide](https://ascribed-dev.com/guides/report/) tells people they can use. When that file has `cache = true`:

- **Every moved link (`link-external-moved`, ASC169) disappears from the second run on.** lychee's cache keeps an address, a status, and a time, and nothing about a redirect. A reused answer comes back as "OK (cached)" with no redirect listed, so Ascribe has nothing to report.
- **lychee writes `.lycheecache` into the project's root,** a file the project didn't ask Ascribe for and probably doesn't ignore.

## To reproduce

With lychee 0.24.2, in a folder holding `lychee.toml` with the one line `cache = true`, give lychee two addresses that redirect, using the arguments Ascribe uses:

```sh
printf 'https://vale.sh/docs/install\nhttps://agentskills.io\n' > u.txt
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # first run
lychee --format json --verbose --no-progress - < u.txt   # second run
```

| Run | `redirects` | `cached` | Entries in `redirect_map` |
|---|---|---|---|
| First | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| Second | 0 | 2 | 0 |

`.lycheecache` then holds `https://vale.sh/docs/install,200,…`: the status, and no sign that it moved.

## Why

`crates/ascribe-check/src/links.rs` starts lychee with `--format json --verbose --no-progress -` and nothing about the cache, so the project's `lychee.toml` decides.

## Fix

Pass `--cache=false` to lychee. A flag on the command line overrides the setting in `lychee.toml` (checked: with it, the file's `cache = true` has no effect and no `.lycheecache` is written).

Also, in `docs/content/guides/report.md`, where it says lychee reads its own `lychee.toml`: say that Ascribe turns lychee's cache off, and why.

A test with the stand-in checker can't show this, since it's about lychee's own behavior. The scheduled Report workflow, or the test that runs a real lychee if there is one, is where to hold it.

## Related

The [cache proposal](https://github.com/ascribed-dev/ascribe/blob/main/project-docs/proposals/cache.md) (not yet on `main` when this was filed) is for Ascribe keeping link results itself, in a form that keeps redirects. This issue is the bug that exists without it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
content.title: `ascribe report links` loses every moved link when a project's lychee.toml turns lychee's cache on
